content.text: Started with a couple small bash scripts, a lot of duplication in these but I think that helps with the understanding of what is being done when looking in the scripts.
https://github.com/whikloj/fedora4-tests
To try them you:
1. Stand up a Fedora4 instance. Using vagrant, webapp-plus or one click.
2. Clone the above repository.
3. Change any variables in the
config
file.
4. Run the individual shell scripts.
It requires curl.
could you try these out and let me know if they are a) too opaque, b) too simple or c) just right.
Also, if you have any problems running them.
- I had no issues running the tests.  They are pretty straight forward and a good start.   Not sure if I'm a good judge of whether or not they are too opaque though, since I am a developer.

The only thing I'd change is to make the tests automatically clean up after themselves each time.  Really only matters in the case where I might want to run this on a repo that I don't plan on throwing away - ie, if a user decides to run this test suite on something other then a RC – which may happen if people use some of this to get an understanding of the API.
I've updated these tests quite a bit over the past couple of days.
I was able to get the fixity test to verify the fixity test result, however I stored the sha-1 result in the test as different machines and OSs will have different ways to generate it.
I added an indirect container test, which uses the pcdm:Collection example to test that the ldp:hasMemberRelation property is added to the ldp:membershipResource pointing to the correct resource.
These matching tests are simple (using grep, sed and string ==) but they work... so far.
- Is there anything else you can think of that we would like to test in this fashion?
Throwing this (
http://www.seleniumhq.org/projects/)
here as an possibility for writing comprehensive HTML UI tests in whatever language you like.
A very simple test using Selenium in Python3 with Firefox.
https://github.com/whikloj/fedora4-tests/tree/html-ui-tests
Suggested to extend to:
check for serialization to disk
indexing to Solr
indexing to Triplestore
Suggestion tooling for JSON interactions
https://stedolan.github.io/jq/
PR for testing the solr and triplestore indexing
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo4-tests/pull/7
New test added in this PR does not pass.
just coming back to this. I'll try running that PR against a vagrant setup of 4.7.1 and report back.
, I just created a new vagrant box with 4.7.1 and was able to run this test either in OS X into the box, or right inside the vagrant box under Ubuntu linux without see the error you described.
Can you give it another try and if there is any additional information please let me know.

vagrant@fedora4:~/fcrepo4-tests$ ./camel_toolbox_tests.sh 

Success may not be immediate, we will wait up to 30 seconds.

Create an object
201 == 201 (Pass)
Checking for item in Solr...............
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/test_camel/object_to_index == http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/test_camel/object_to_index (Pass)
Checking for item in Triplestore.....
Object 1 == Object 1 (Pass)
All tests completed
Remove any test objects created? (Y/n) 
Deleting http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/test_camel
vagrant@fedora4:~/fcrepo4-tests$ uname -a
Linux fedora4 3.13.0-87-generic #133-Ubuntu SMP Tue May 24 18:32:09 UTC 2016 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo4-tests/commit/f3a6393853c6cdd759fd42c2fcf03fd316c2db6b
From a Fedora Tech Meeting on March 31st, 2016.

The goal of this issue is to create a way to automatically test release candidates as well as have a subset of those tests be available to be done manually. The subset of the tests which could be manually performed would be available to help new users learn how to work with the Fedora4 API.
The conversation focused creating a tool (TCK/script) that can be run to automatically test a release candidate, based on the list on the testing procedure pages [1][2].
Part of the tests in the tool could be exposed via some mechanism (HTML?) and made available for new users to learn how to use the Fedora4 API.
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/Release+Testing+-+4.5.1
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/Release+Testing+Procedures
